findingDetails.case: The caller supplies a marked scratch directory outside the repository whose child named for the selected runtime is a symlink to the repository root.

claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The project is intended to be created below scratch and the marker may appear to establish ownership; however mkdirp and marker writes follow an existing runtime-child symlink, and the later realpath comparison uses that target as the project boundary.
claimAdjudication.claim: A runtime child symlink can redirect the project root into the repository before the current containment checks run.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Re-read the complete scratch guard, path resolution helpers, adapter launches, REQ-001, and refusal tests; no check resolves the project root against repoPath or scratchPath before marker/setup. The linked specs-leaf test does not cover a symlink at scratch/runtime.

findingDetails.evidence: The guard checks only scratchPath against repoPath, then writes through scratchPath/runtime and runs setup there. It later sets projectReal to the symlink target and checks specs/state only relative to projectReal, so a repository-root target satisfies those checks.

findingDetails.title: A runtime-project symlink bypasses the scratch boundary

findingDetails.case: A setup command is still running when the operator sends SIGINT or SIGTERM.

claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The setup timeout kills the command group on timeout, but it does not cover an external signal that calls cleanupAll and process.exit before the timeout callback.

findingDetails.evidence: runBoundedCommand spawns a detached bash process but adds its PID to cleanup state only when ctx exists. main awaits guardScratch without passing ctx, while signal handlers call cleanupAll over active runtime contexts and immediately exit.

findingDetails.case: A Codex scenario asks the model to read or write an absolute path outside the selected scratch project.

claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The process starts with cwd set to scratch and the spec treats that guard as confinement; a working directory selects relative paths but does not constrain absolute paths or commands when the CLI sandbox is explicitly bypassed.
claimAdjudication.claim: The Codex adapter disables its own sandbox while the runner supplies only a working directory, leaving the host filesystem unrestricted by this runner.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Re-read Codex launch/resume, the tmux subject launcher, repository snapshot scope, NFR-S02 and the adapter plan. No container or OS sandbox wrapper exists. The official Codex CLI source marks this flag extremely dangerous and intended only for externally sandboxed environments.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade only when the launched Codex process is externally confined to the scratch project and a regression proves absolute writes outside scratch are denied.

findingDetails.evidence: Codex is launched and resumed with --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox. The runner passes the scratch path as tmux's working directory but does not put the child in an external filesystem sandbox. The repository snapshot observes only specs and configured state subfolders after the run, so it neither confines nor prevents other host writes.
findingDetails.recommendation: Run the CLI inside an externally enforced filesystem sandbox/container that preserves required tmux IPC, or remove this launch mode and keep filesystem restrictions enabled.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The Codex adapter passes the explicit bypass flag. startSubject supplies only tmux cwd and argv; no container, OS sandbox, or path restriction wraps the process.
findingDetails.title: Codex runs without a host filesystem sandbox
findingDetails.userImpact: The live model can alter or read user and repository files outside scratch without an approval prompt; later detection of selected repository changes cannot undo those effects.

findingDetails.case: A monitored directory is searchable/writable by the runner user but not readable, such as a known state directory with write and execute but no read permission; a check writes a known file path in it.

claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The catch may be intended to tolerate absent optional roots, but it also suppresses EACCES and other traversal errors for roots that the contract says must be hashed.
claimAdjudication.claim: The repository snapshot silently omits monitored directories when traversal fails, allowing changes in writable omitted paths to escape comparison.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Re-read the walker, snapshot producer, and REQ-008. Missing and unreadable roots share the same catch-and-return behavior; there is no warning or failed snapshot result.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if traversal returns typed completeness evidence and unreadable monitored roots fail the run, with a regression for a writable but unreadable watched directory.

findingDetails.evidence: walkFiles returns an empty contribution for any readdirSync error. If the same unreadable root is omitted from both snapshots, a subject can append to a known writable file without a path, size, or hash row changing because no row was ever captured.
findingDetails.recommendation: Distinguish expected missing roots from unreadable or failed traversal and fail the run closed when any monitored subtree cannot be completely enumerated or hashed.
findingDetails.scopeProof: snapshotRepo uses walkFiles for specs and every configured state root; one shared catch swallows readdir errors on every recursion branch, with no incomplete-snapshot signal.
findingDetails.title: Unreadable snapshot subtrees are treated as empty
findingDetails.userImpact: The repository-integrity check can silently report unchanged state after a write to an omitted watched file.

findingDetails.scopeProof: restoreHookTrust iterates only current tables and verifies only additions and changed tables; the hook-trust regression covers additions and body changes but not a pre-existing table removed during the run.
findingDetails.title: Removed pre-existing project hook trust is not restored

findingDetails.case: The caller supplies a marked scratch directory outside the repository whose child named for the selected runtime is a symlink to the repository root.

claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The project is intended to be created below scratch and the marker may appear to establish ownership; however mkdirp and marker writes follow an existing runtime-child symlink, and the later realpath comparison uses that target as the project boundary.
claimAdjudication.claim: A runtime child symlink can redirect the project root into the repository before the current containment checks run.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Re-read the complete scratch guard, path resolution helpers, adapter launches, REQ-001, and refusal tests; no check resolves the project root against repoPath or scratchPath before marker/setup. The linked specs-leaf test does not cover a symlink at scratch/runtime.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if the guard resolves the runtime project before any write, rejects project roots inside the repository or outside the canonical scratch root, and a regression test covers scratch/runtime -> repository.

findingDetails.evidence: The guard checks only scratchPath against repoPath, then writes through scratchPath/runtime and runs setup there. It later sets projectReal to the symlink target and checks specs/state only relative to projectReal, so a repository-root target satisfies those checks.
findingDetails.recommendation: Resolve and verify the runtime project itself is outside the repository before writing its marker or running setup; reject symlinked project roots that escape the approved scratch root.
findingDetails.scopeProof: One shared guardScratch implementation feeds all five runtime adapters; the adapter table at lines 1008-1112 launches Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex, Pi, and Devin, while refusal tests cover a scratch parent inside the repo and a linked specs leaf but not a linked runtime project.
findingDetails.title: A runtime-project symlink bypasses the scratch boundary
findingDetails.userImpact: A runtime launched with approval and sandbox bypass flags can run with the repository as its working project and write packet or repository data despite the scratch-only safety contract.

findingDetails.case: A setup command is still running when the operator sends SIGINT or SIGTERM.

claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The setup timeout kills the command group on timeout, but it does not cover an external signal that calls cleanupAll and process.exit before the timeout callback.
claimAdjudication.claim: A signal during main's setup phase can exit before the detached setup child is registered for cleanup.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Re-read child tracking, cleanupAll, SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers, main's guard call, and the signal regression. The test covers interruption after subject start, not during setup.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if a signal during a blocking setup command kills and verifies the entire detached process group and a regression covers both SIGINT and SIGTERM before runtime activation.

findingDetails.evidence: runBoundedCommand spawns a detached bash process but adds its PID to cleanup state only when ctx exists. main awaits guardScratch without passing ctx, while signal handlers call cleanupAll over active runtime contexts and immediately exit.
findingDetails.recommendation: Track setup child process groups in a context registered before setup starts, and have signal cleanup terminate and verify those groups before exiting.
findingDetails.scopeProof: All setup commands enter runBoundedCommand from guardScratch; main calls guardScratch without ctx, and child tracking is conditional on ctx.children. The only SIGINT regression waits until the subject has started, after runRuntime has registered an active context.
findingDetails.title: SIGINT during setup leaves the detached setup child running
findingDetails.userImpact: The runner can exit while a setup process or its descendants continue running, violating the promised cleanup and potentially continuing setup writes after the run has been interrupted.

findingDetails.case: A setup command writes a file under specs or a watched state subtree and exits successfully.

claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: Setup is preparation rather than the interactive runtime; however the workflow runs setup as part of each selected runtime's execution, exposes the repository root to it, and REQ-008 requires repository changes from a run to fail.
claimAdjudication.claim: Repository changes made by setup commands are absent from the before/after comparison because the baseline is captured only after setup returns.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Re-read the setup flow, environment passed to setup, snapshot timing, and REQ-008. The runtime snapshot regression covers a check-time append, but not setup-time changes.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if the contract expressly excludes setup from repository-integrity checks and setup is made read-only, or if a pre-setup baseline detects setup mutations.

findingDetails.evidence: main awaits guardScratch, which runs setup with CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT, before runRuntime creates its context and writes repo-before.txt from snapshotRepo. The later comparison therefore starts after any setup mutation and can report the unchanged post-setup state as clean.
findingDetails.recommendation: Capture a repository baseline before setup begins and compare it after setup and the runtime, or explicitly constrain setup to read-only repository access and enforce that boundary.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The single pre-run ordering is main -> guardScratch/setup -> runRuntime -> snapshotRepo. The setup interface explicitly receives CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT, and no snapshot is taken in guardScratch.
findingDetails.title: Setup-time repository writes occur before the baseline snapshot
findingDetails.userImpact: A run can report no repository change even though its setup phase changed a watched file, weakening the snapshot's fail-on-change guarantee.

findingDetails.case: A Codex scenario asks the model to read or write an absolute path outside the selected scratch project.

claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The process starts with cwd set to scratch and the spec treats that guard as confinement; a working directory selects relative paths but does not constrain absolute paths or commands when the CLI sandbox is explicitly bypassed.
claimAdjudication.claim: The Codex adapter disables its own sandbox while the runner supplies only a working directory, leaving the host filesystem unrestricted by this runner.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Re-read Codex launch/resume, the tmux subject launcher, repository snapshot scope, NFR-S02 and the adapter plan. No container or OS sandbox wrapper exists. The official Codex CLI source marks this flag extremely dangerous and intended only for externally sandboxed environments.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade only when the launched Codex process is externally confined to the scratch project and a regression proves absolute writes outside scratch are denied.

findingDetails.evidence: Codex is launched and resumed with --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox. The runner passes the scratch path as tmux's working directory but does not put the child in an external filesystem sandbox. The repository snapshot observes only specs and configured state subfolders after the run, so it neither confines nor prevents other host writes.
findingDetails.recommendation: Run the CLI inside an externally enforced filesystem sandbox/container that preserves required tmux IPC, or remove this launch mode and keep filesystem restrictions enabled.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The Codex adapter passes the explicit bypass flag. startSubject supplies only tmux cwd and argv; no container, OS sandbox, or path restriction wraps the process.
findingDetails.title: Codex runs without a host filesystem sandbox
findingDetails.userImpact: The live model can alter or read user and repository files outside scratch without an approval prompt; later detection of selected repository changes cannot undo those effects.

findingDetails.case: A monitored directory is searchable/writable by the runner user but not readable, such as a known state directory with write and execute but no read permission; a check writes a known file path in it.

claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The catch may be intended to tolerate absent optional roots, but it also suppresses EACCES and other traversal errors for roots that the contract says must be hashed.
claimAdjudication.claim: The repository snapshot silently omits monitored directories when traversal fails, allowing changes in writable omitted paths to escape comparison.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Re-read the walker, snapshot producer, and REQ-008. Missing and unreadable roots share the same catch-and-return behavior; there is no warning or failed snapshot result.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if traversal returns typed completeness evidence and unreadable monitored roots fail the run, with a regression for a writable but unreadable watched directory.

findingDetails.evidence: walkFiles returns an empty contribution for any readdirSync error. If the same unreadable root is omitted from both snapshots, a subject can append to a known writable file without a path, size, or hash row changing because no row was ever captured.
findingDetails.recommendation: Distinguish expected missing roots from unreadable or failed traversal and fail the run closed when any monitored subtree cannot be completely enumerated or hashed.
findingDetails.scopeProof: snapshotRepo uses walkFiles for specs and every configured state root; one shared catch swallows readdir errors on every recursion branch, with no incomplete-snapshot signal.
findingDetails.title: Unreadable snapshot subtrees are treated as empty
findingDetails.userImpact: The repository-integrity check can silently report unchanged state after a write to an omitted watched file.

findingDetails.case: A reused scratch project's pre-existing hooks.state table disappears from the user's Codex config during a trust-enabled run.

claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: The expected Codex flow appears to add or change trust tables, which is what the regression models; however removal of a pre-existing table is a possible config mutation and is not included in the claimed restoration audit.
claimAdjudication.claim: The hook trust restorer does not reinstate a pre-existing project table that is deleted during the run and can still report ok.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Re-read snapshot capture, the full current-table and restoration loops, final ok computation, and the trust regression. The code never iterates snapshot project keys missing from currentTables.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Close if the trust contract explicitly excludes restoration of removed pre-existing scratch-project tables, or if code restores them and the regression covers deletion.

findingDetails.evidence: A missing table is absent from currentTables and therefore never enters added or changed. Post-restore validation checks that additions were removed and changed bodies were restored, but does not verify that every pre-run project table still exists; ok can remain true.
findingDetails.recommendation: Compare the post-run project table set with the snapshot and restore or report any missing pre-existing project table.
findingDetails.scopeProof: restoreHookTrust iterates only current tables and verifies only additions and changed tables; the hook-trust regression covers additions and body changes but not a pre-existing table removed during the run.
findingDetails.title: Removed pre-existing project hook trust is not restored
findingDetails.userImpact: The run can report successful hook-trust cleanup while leaving the user's existing trust decision for that scratch project deleted.

findingDetails.case: A reviewer relies on AC-005's Met status as evidence that writes to both specs and watched state paths are detected.
findingDetails.evidence: AC-005 says its evidence covers a fake run writing under specs and a separate append to watched state. The only repoChanged test creates one check that appends to decision-capture/queue.md; no specs write appears in that case or elsewhere in the bound runner test.
findingDetails.recommendation: Add evidence for a fake write under specs or narrow AC-005's Given/verification statement to the state-path case actually covered.
findingDetails.scopeProof: The only repoChanged regression in the bound test file appends to a watched state queue. Search for REPO_CHANGED and CONVERSATION_REPO_ROOT specs writes found no test for the distinct specs subtree case described in AC-005.
findingDetails.title: AC-005 is marked Met without evidence for its specs write case
findingDetails.userImpact: The acceptance record overstates the exercised snapshot coverage, so a regression that omits the specs root could pass the recorded evidence gate.

findingDetails.case: A setup or check command starts a descendant that moves to another process group/session, or a timed-out child group has not fully exited when finish runs.

claimAdjudication.alternativeExplanation: SIGKILL should terminate members still in the original process group, but a command can create a new session/group, and the timeout path drops tracking before close or descendant verification.
claimAdjudication.claim: The runner does not verify setup/check child groups after signaling them and can report childrenGone=true while an escaped or not-yet-exited descendant remains.
claimAdjudication.counterevidenceSought: Re-read process-group kill, timeout finish, cleanupContext, groupAlive, terminateGroup, timeout regression, and REQ-006/007. Pane descendants are polled, but setup/check child groups are not; timeout coverage uses only sleep 30.
claimAdjudication.downgradeTrigger: Downgrade if a detached-descendant timeout test proves no child remains and cleanup reports failure when descendant verification fails.

findingDetails.evidence: The timeout handler sends SIGKILL to the original process group and immediately calls finish; finish deletes the child PID from ctx.children before observing close. cleanupContext then kills whatever tracked PIDs remain, clears the set, and sets childrenGone=true without a survivor check. Only the pane process group is polled with pgrep.
findingDetails.recommendation: Keep timed-out child groups tracked until close, verify their process groups and descendants are gone before setting childrenGone, and return CLEANUP_INCOMPLETE when verification fails.
findingDetails.scopeProof: All setup/check commands use runBoundedCommand. The timeout path signals a process group and immediately calls finish, which removes the PID; cleanupContext separately clears tracked child PIDs and hardcodes childrenGone=true.
findingDetails.title: Cleanup reports child processes gone without verification
findingDetails.userImpact: A command descendant can continue after timeout or run cleanup, potentially writing after the repository snapshot and leaving the runner's own process alive while the result reports cleanup complete.
